# Rebase plan: #201 onto new base (effort support + node selections)

In this rebase "ours" is the new base and "theirs" is the replayed #201 commit. The new base adds configured reasoning effort (`--effort` for Claude, `model_reasoning_effort` for Codex) and records node selections. #201 adds command-scoped inspection reuse. Both sides are kept in all three files; neither replaces the other.

## internal/agent/adapters_test.go

Ours: Appends `TestAgentEffortHelper`, `TestEffortArgvMapsOnlySupportedFlag`, `TestConfiguredRunnerRejectsInvalidEffort` and `TestConfiguredEffortReachesHarnessAndProvenance` after the last base test. These cover effort argv mapping, rejection of unsupported effort values, and effort reaching the harness and provenance. Imports stay the same (`slices` is already imported).

Theirs: Adds `runtime` and `internal/sandbox` imports, and appends `countedCalls`, `TestInspectionTrustedLocalOpenCodeCallers` (preflight for both roles plus launch share one inspection; changed approved config re-inspects; a nil session stays uncached) and `TestInspectionIsolatedCodexPreflightToLaunch` (version inspected once, canary/auth run every time, unauthorized role is still rejected, a failing canary stops a cache hit) at the same spot.

Resolution: Keep both sets of appended tests, one after the other: ours's effort tests first, then theirs's inspection tests. Remove the markers. Keep the merged import block that is already there (`runtime`, `slices`, `sandbox`). Keep every test as written on both sides, with no edits to assertions. If ours's effort test runs through a session-aware path, it still needs to pass with a nil session, as written.

Approved behavior: Keeps the plan's required coverage for reuse within one session, invalidation when policy changes, nil-session uncached callers, role authorization on every preflight, and canaries that are never cached. The new base's effort tests also stay, so the rebase loses no coverage.

## internal/cli/node.go

Ours: Declares `var selections []map[string]any` next to `pauses`/`splits`. After each successful `pullNextReadyIssue` it appends `{repo, issue_number, overlap}` under `outputMu`, and adds `"selections"` to both the failed and drained node JSON outputs. `execute` keeps the signature `func(pulled)`.

Theirs: Changes `execute` to `func(ctx context.Context, pulled)` and adds the `context` import. Each claimed task in a worker loop gets a fresh `taskCtx := sandbox.WithInspectionSession(ctx, sandbox.NewInspectionSession())`, which is used for both `pullNextReadyIssue` and `execute(taskCtx, pulled)`. That way each task is its own command lifetime and nothing is reused across tasks.

Resolution: Hunk 1 keeps `var selections []map[string]any` and also takes theirs's `execute := func(ctx context.Context, pulled *pulledWorkUnit)`. Hunk 2 keeps ours's locked `selections` append right after a successful pull, then calls `execute(taskCtx, pulled)`. Keep theirs's `taskCtx` creation before the pull, keep the `context` import, and keep ours's `"selections"` keys in both JSON outputs (they are already merged outside the markers). The `selections` append stays on the worker goroutine under `outputMu` and does not touch `taskCtx`.

Approved behavior: The inspection session is still owned by one command per claimed task and thrown away afterwards, as the plan requires for node/reused Engine executions. Selection preflight and execution share that one session, and no global or cross-task cache appears. Ours's selection reporting does not change, and no CLI flag or contract changes are added.

## internal/sandbox/delegated.go

Ours: Splits `InspectDelegatedHarness` into an exported wrapper and an unexported `inspectDelegatedHarness(ctx, driver, binary, extra []string)` that also checks for extra help flags. `RunDelegatedHarness` passes `extra = []string{"--effort"}` when `driver == "claude" && opts.Effort != ""`, so an older Claude fails before work starts. Isolated Claude argv moves into `claudeArgs(config, settings, model, effort)`.

Theirs: Changes the launch-time inspection in `RunDelegatedHarness` to `opts.Inspections.InspectDelegatedHarness(ctx, driver, binary, opts.InspectionPolicy)`, a session-aware lookup that is uncached when the session is nil. Executor and Claude authentication checks still run after it every time.

Resolution: Keep ours's wrapper/helper split, the `extra` computation and `claudeArgs`. The launch call becomes a session-aware inspection that also gets ours's `extra` flags, e.g. `opts.Inspections.InspectDelegatedHarness(ctx, driver, binary, opts.InspectionPolicy, extra)`. Change the session method (from #201, in `internal/sandbox/native.go`, which is not conflicted) to match:
- With a nil session it delegates to `inspectDelegatedHarness(..., extra)`.
- On a miss, `inspectDelegatedHarness` must fully pass the base flags and `extra` before anything is cached.
- A hit must never satisfy a lookup that needs more flags than were checked. The recommended fix keeps the approved key exactly as it is (driver, canonical path, size, mtime ns, SHA-256, approved-config digest): cache the qualified version together with the help text, and check base+`extra` flags against it on every lookup. If that is impractical, add the required-flag set to the stored entry and re-inspect when it differs.

A cached result from a Claude agent without effort must not let another Claude agent with effort skip the `--effort` check, even when both use the same binary and the same approved config. The exported `InspectDelegatedHarness` stays uncached and fully checked with `extra=nil`. Also check that the preclaim delegated call in `internal/agent/configured.go`, which is now on the session path, passes the same `extra` that ours requires at launch, so the effort mismatch still stops before a claim.

Approved behavior: Only successful interface qualification is cached. Changed identity or policy still re-inspects. A failed or under-qualified inspection returns an error, never a stale result. The tool executor and Claude authentication still run on every launch, and the exported wrappers stay uncached. Ours's fail-early effort qualification is kept for both cached and uncached callers, so isolation never falls back and a mismatched harness stops before work is claimed.

Shape: **Involved** — inspection spans command selection, workflow preflight and sandbox launch; native inspection currently combines reusable interface checks with mandatory canaries.

## What we know
- `internal/agent/configured.go:126` authorizes each role, then inspects; `internal/workflow/engine.go:411` repeats this per role.
- `internal/sandbox/native.go:175` combines version/help qualification and filesystem/network canaries; `:283` repeats inspection at launch. `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:18` checks interfaces; `:95` repeats inspection but separately checks the tool executor and authentication.
- #199 timing exists: `internal/sandbox/lifecycle.go:8` feeds `internal/agent/telemetry.go:463` and `internal/contract/telemetry.go:48` (`preflight_ms`). It measures role launch, not the earlier workflow preclaim loop.
- PR overrides preflight before engine preflight (`internal/pr/service.go:689`); selection also preflights (`internal/cli/selection.go:134`). Engine options currently carry only environment/profile context (`internal/workflow/engine.go:176`).

## Alternatives
- Cache in `sandbox`, with command-owned plumbing from the agent/workflow layers. Reject caching all of `PreflightWithOptions` or `CLIAdapter.Run`: those include role authorization, authentication and boundary checks that must run every time, and would miss sandbox launch reuse.
- Include SHA-256 content identity. Reject path+size+mtime alone because same-size replacements can preserve timestamps. Hashing a large Codex binary on every lookup costs I/O; measure that cost against saved subprocess time, and reopen if benefit is negligible.
- Retain preclaim inspection and reuse its interface result at launch. Reject launch-only inspection because failures must stop before a claim.

## Exact cache inputs
Inspection itself takes **no approved policy input**: `InspectNativeCodex(ctx, binary)` and `InspectDelegatedHarness(ctx, driver, binary)` qualify version/help with `nativeEnv(home, false, Dependencies{})` in a temporary empty home (`native.go:203`, `delegated.go:29`). Role, model, permissions, dependencies and credentials do not parameterize that qualification; authentication and canaries remain outside the cache.

For conservative compliance with policy invalidation, the session-aware cache key is exactly: driver (`codex`, `claude`, `opencode`, `omp`), resolved canonical absolute executable path, file size, modification time in nanoseconds, SHA-256 of executable bytes, and SHA-256 of `encoding/json.Marshal` of the complete approved `contract.SwarmConfig`. Include **all serialized config fields** (`Execution`, `Version`, `DefaultAgent`, `DefaultGate`, `PlanMode`, `CommitMessage`, `LedgerNamespace`, `Roles`, `Lease`, `Security`, `Agents`, `Fork`, including their serialized nested fields; `internal/contract/types.go:125`), including zero values as encoded by their existing JSON tags; no selected-field whitelist, candidate config, role name, or extra implicit “relevant policy” input. Marshal errors fail closed. This last digest is a conservative partition, not an input to inspection. Different approved config content re-inspects even when the changed field would not affect interface qualification. Build this partition from the existing approved-base config before constructing each runner, and carry it unchanged to launch; no new policy load from the candidate. If an invocation changes approved config, recompute the partition rather than retaining the old digest. Nil-session exported APIs take no partition and stay uncached.

## Implementation sequence
1. Measure an unchanged repository workflow first. Use #199 per-role `preflight_ms`, plus narrowly scoped coordinator timers around preclaim preflight and version/interface inspection. Record repeated same-policy runs, role, harness/version, sampling method and native inspection duration in IMPLEMENTATION.md for the PR. Avoid credentials and local identity/path details. Repeat identical measurements after; explain materiality and hashing/canary costs. Fixtures establish correctness, not real-harness performance.
2. Add a command-owned, concurrency-safe inspection session in existing `internal/sandbox/native.go`; pass it through existing `RunnerOptions`/`CLIAdapter` (`internal/agent/configured.go`, `adapters.go`), `WorkerOptions` (`internal/sandbox/worker.go`) and `internal/agent/isolated.go`. Thread invocation ownership through `internal/cli/work.go`, `selection.go`, `internal/workflow/engine.go` and `internal/pr/service.go`, including PR override preflight and subsequent execution. Discard it after the command, including node/reused Engine or Service executions. Nil session preserves uncached callers. No package-global or persistent cache.
3. Split native version/help qualification from canaries in `native.go`; cache only successful interface/version inspection for native Codex and delegated Claude/OpenCode/omp in `delegated.go`. Keep existing exported inspection wrappers fully checking boundaries. Key reuse by canonical executable path, size, nanosecond mtime, SHA-256 content hash, driver, and the complete approved-config digest defined above. Check identity on every lookup, including same-size/same-mtime replacement; verify identity before/after inspection and reject unstable files. Changed stable identity/policy re-inspects; unreadable, unstable or failed inspection returns an error, never a stale result. Never cache authorization, authentication, runtime checks, role-specific permissions or canaries. OCI remains unchanged. Recheck at launch as today.
4. Extend existing tests below, add the changelog fragment, then validate. No contract/schema/CLI flag changes. Retain current telemetry meanings; any supplementary inspection timing stays internal and is reported in IMPLEMENTATION.md.

## Inspection caller coverage
All cached entries below cache only successful interface qualification; native canaries still execute on every call. “Session-aware” means cached only when a command supplies a session; nil remains uncached.

| Caller | Treatment |
|---|---|
| `internal/agent/configured.go:138/151` native/delegated preclaim | Session-aware, after per-role authorization; auth and executor checks unchanged. |
| `internal/agent/configured.go:200` trusted-local OpenCode via `r.Available()` | Session-aware, using the resolved available executable and same approved-config partition. |
| `internal/agent/adapters.go:173` non-isolated OpenCode launch | Session-aware; share with trusted-local preclaim. |
| `internal/sandbox/native.go:284` `RunNativeCodex` | Session-aware via `WorkerOptions`; rerun canaries and authentication. |
| `internal/sandbox/delegated.go:96` `RunDelegatedHarness` | Session-aware via `WorkerOptions`; rerun executor/authentication checks. |
| `internal/sandbox/native.go:170` `CheckNativeCodex` | Uncached; retain exported `InspectNativeCodex` and full version/help plus boundary checks. |
| `internal/sandbox/native.go:323` `RunNativeValidation` | Uncached through `CheckNativeCodex`; full checks every invocation. |
| `internal/sandbox/validation.go:29` `CheckNativeValidation` | Uncached through `CheckNativeCodex`; full checks every invocation. Non-Codex executor checks unchanged. |
| Direct exported inspection callers, doctor and existing harness integration fixtures | Uncached and fully checked; no global/session lookup hidden in wrappers. |

## Assumptions and open questions
Real authenticated native execution and before/after timing may require the operator's Linux environment. Probe availability during step 1; if unavailable, record the exact measurement gap for PR review and supply reproducible steps, without blocking sandbox-verifiable implementation. AC1 remains unsatisfied until actual before/after per-role measurements are attached to the PR; a gap alone is not acceptance evidence. If caching version/help alone has negligible benefit, report that evidence and reopen the scope decision; never cache canaries to obtain a speedup. The cycle should fit the 16-hour budget.

Approved-base file absence cannot be proven here: this mounted snapshot has no `.git` metadata (`git rev-parse HEAD` fails). All listed source/test files exist and are **modified**, not new. The sole proposed added repository file, `changes/unreleased/201-preflight-inspection.md`, is absent from this snapshot; verify absence with `git cat-file -e "$base_sha:changes/unreleased/201-preflight-inspection.md"` against the authoritative approved base in the coordinator checkout before describing it as new. Do not infer approved-base identity from the mount.

## HANDOFF
- Caller classification: the table above is exhaustive for current production inspection callers, including trusted-local OpenCode and both uncached validation paths. Add session-aware helpers without changing exported uncached wrappers.
- Entry points/symbols: `PreflightWithOptions` (`configured.go:126`), `CLIAdapter.Run` (`adapters.go:153`), `runIsolated` (`isolated.go:18`), `InspectNativeCodex`/`RunNativeCodex` (`native.go:175/:282`), `InspectDelegatedHarness`/`RunDelegatedHarness` (`delegated.go:18/:94`), `Engine.runnerOptions` (`engine.go:189`), and preclaim call sites above. Paths without directories here are relative to their packages above.
- Extend `internal/sandbox/native_test.go`, `lifecycle_test.go`, `internal/agent/adapters_test.go`, `telemetry_test.go`, `internal/workflow/engine_test.go`, `reviewer_policy_test.go`, `internal/pr/service_test.go`, and `internal/cli/execution_test.go`. Use counting fake executables; preserve real boundary fixtures in `native_test.go` and `harness_integration_test.go`.
- Focused commands and acceptance mapping: TEST_PLAN.md. Run build and changed-package vet before targeted tests as specified there; record current results rather than relying on prior-run reports.
- What this change breaks: inspection callers listed above require session plumbing; direct `agent.Preflight`, doctor (`internal/cli/doctor.go:73`), and exported sandbox inspection callers retain uncached/full-check semantics. Preserve telemetry null/zero assertions and native boundary/cancellation/import tests. Search found no docs referring to `preflight_ms`; no existing docs/templates need edits. Add only the changelog fragment for user-facing documentation.
- Reopen for policy ambiguity, inability to maintain command lifetime or mandatory canaries, required protected-file changes, or negligible measured benefit. Developer writes only source, tests, docs, IMPLEMENTATION.md and LESSONS.md; modifying any other active artifact discards the run. Do not restage/rewrite PLAN.md, TEST_PLAN.md or other active inputs.

1. **Measured per-role before/after:** Before editing, capture #199 role `preflight_ms` for the same repository workflow, harness, executable and approved policy; separately time preclaim preflight and native/interface inspection. Repeat several samples before/after with fresh command sessions; report per-role samples/medians and inspection counts in IMPLEMENTATION.md and the PR. Confirm canary/auth counts stay unchanged. Real-harness access gaps go in PR review notes; neither gaps nor mock times satisfy this criterion. Include hashing overhead for the real executable and reopen the plan if net benefit is negligible.
2. **Reuse, invalidation and safety:** Extend existing sandbox/agent tests with counting fake executables: shared executable/policy across roles executes version/help once; different canonical path, size, mtime, same-size/same-mtime changed hash, driver, and approved-config digest each re-inspect (change a serialized approved config field, e.g. DefaultAgent, without changing the selected executable; also verify identical config values in a different allocation reuse). Independent command sessions never share. Name the new cases `TestInspectionSymlinkRetargeting` and `TestInspectionSameSizeSameMtimeReplacement` so the focused pattern runs both. Cover symlink retargeting, missing/unreadable executable, mutation during inspection, failures not cached, cancelled inspection and concurrent requests (race detector). Confirm every role still authorizes and authenticates, runs native filesystem/network and delegated executor canaries, and rejects a failing canary even on a cache hit. Extend workflow/PR/CLI tests to cover preclaim-to-launch reuse, override preflight, reused Engine/Service command isolation and no claim on failed/stale inspection. Exercise both trusted-local OpenCode callers (`configured.go:200`, `adapters.go:173`) with shared-session reuse and nil-session repeated inspection. Test `CheckNativeCodex`, `RunNativeValidation`, and `CheckNativeValidation` with counting fixtures: every invocation repeats version/help and native boundary canaries even after the same binary was cached by a worker session; a subsequent failed interface or canary must fail validation. Preserve direct uncached API behavior, OCI behavior, reviewer restrictions, telemetry field semantics and existing boundary tests.
3. **Build/check acceptance and changelog:** Verify the fragment is absent at the approved base before adding it; review its text against actual behavior. Run, in order:

```bash
go build ./...
go vet ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr ./internal/cli
go test -race ./internal/sandbox ./internal/agent ./internal/workflow ./internal/pr ./internal/cli -run 'Test.*(Inspection|Preflight|Telemetry|Native|CommandSession)' -count=1
make check
```

Use those names for added focused tests and include existing regressions matched above. Run additional changed-package targeted cases if their names are outside the pattern. `make check` is the single full suite: it includes formatting, whole-repository vet/staticcheck and `go test -race ./...`; do not also run `go test ./...` or `make install`. Report environmental failures with exact diagnostics; never weaken tests or boundaries.

Planner revision verification: `go build ./...`, the changed-package vet command above, and the targeted race-test command above all passed on this snapshot. No full suite was run during this plan revision; implementation must still satisfy `make check`. Only PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md were edited.

VERDICT: APPROVED

Shape **Involved** fits: the change spans the sandbox, agent, workflow, PR and CLI layers and splits a security-relevant function. The plan lists rejected alternatives and has a measurement step. It meets all three required operator revisions.

| Item | Status | Evidence |

| Objective: measure per-role preflight/inspection | Covered | Plan step 1; TEST_PLAN §1. It states plainly that AC1 is unmet until real before/after numbers are attached to the PR. |
| Objective: command-scoped cache keyed by executable identity + policy | Covered | "Exact cache inputs" gives the key: driver, canonical path, size, mtime in ns, SHA-256 of the bytes, SHA-256 of the full approved `SwarmConfig`. It says plainly that inspection takes no policy input (verified: `native.go:197/205` and `delegated.go:27` use `nativeEnv(home, false, Dependencies{})` in a temp home). |
| Out of scope: no persistent cache | Covered | "No package-global or persistent cache"; nil session stays uncached. |
| Out of scope: never skip authorization or canaries | Covered | Only version/help is cached. Native canaries (`native.go:212-254`), `CheckToolExecutor`, authentication and `validate` still run on every call. |
| Constraint: failed or stale inspection stops before claiming work | Covered | Preclaim inspection is kept; unstable, unreadable or failed lookups return errors and are never cached; the test plan includes no-claim-on-failure tests. |
| Constraint: changelog fragment | Covered | `changes/unreleased/201-preflight-inspection.md` (absent from this snapshot, verified). |
| AC2: reuse, each invalidation, canaries still run | Covered | TEST_PLAN §2 covers path, size, mtime, same-size/same-mtime hash change, driver, config digest, symlink retargeting, concurrency, cancellation, and canary failure on a cache hit. |
| AC3: `make check` | Covered | TEST_PLAN §3 runs `make check` as the single full suite (the `check` target exists in the Makefile). |
| Operator: alternatives listed | Done | Three rejected alternatives, each with a one-line reason. |
| Operator: classify each caller | Done | `configured.go:200` and `adapters.go:173` are cached (session-aware). `native.go:170`, `native.go:323` and `validation.go:29` are uncached and fully checked. Grep confirms the table lists every production caller (`engine.go:432` reaches it through `CheckNativeValidation`). |
| Protected paths | Clean | No protected files are touched; no contract, schema or CLI-flag changes. |

## Notes for the developer (non-blocking)
1. Hashing the Codex binary on every lookup can cost as much as the `--version` / `exec --help` subprocesses it saves. Report hash time next to inspection time in IMPLEMENTATION.md. If the net gain is negligible, reopen as the plan says. Do not drop the hash.
2. `json.Marshal` sorts map keys, so the `Roles` and `Agents` digest is deterministic. Still keep the "identical values in a different allocation reuse" test so this is guaranteed by a test.
3. Exported `InspectNativeCodex`, `InspectDelegatedHarness`, `CheckNativeCodex` and `CheckNativeValidation` must keep their current signatures and full-check behaviour. Put the session-aware path in new unexported or session-method helpers so validation cannot pick up a cached result by accident.
4. If this sandbox cannot run a real harness, record the measurement gap with exact steps to reproduce. Do not substitute fixture timings for AC1.
